item.title: Deadlock at UN climate summit in Turkey
item.description:
The COP31 summit has gone into a second day of overtime after talks were suspended for the night. There is no agreement in sight with the European Union and Pacific Island nations threatening to walk away without agreeing to a deal because the draft text makes no mention of reducing global demand for fossil fuels. Also: Croatians take to the streets over the death in hospital of a psychiatric patient who was beaten and smothered. We hear from British endurance athlete Lewis Pugh who swam through the Strait of Hormuz to highlight the environmental cost of the war between the US and Iran. Nepal's Prime Minister Balendra Shah visits India to try to secure much needed financial aid following devastating floods in the Himalayan nation. And has a maths problem that has puzzled humans for 167 years finally been solved?

item.title: The Happy Pod: The 'amazing’ device that controls Tourette's
item.description:
We meet 17-year-old Mylo who's taken part in a trial of the watch-like device that suppresses his Tourette's tics. He can even now go to the cinema without fear of causing a disturbance by constantly moving or clearing his throat. Also: the chef in Japan who's known poverty and illness and now offers free meals to people in the position he was once in; the NASA spacecraft, Voyager One, that's become the first human-made object to reach a point one light day from Earth; the surf school in Senegal that's trying to turn its pupils into world champions; and the children with autism and ADHD who've been helped by alpacas.

Image: 17-year-old Mylo wearing the device. Credit: BBC News.

Our weekly collection of inspiring, uplifting and happy news from around the world.

Presenter: Holly Gibbs. Music composed by Iona Hampson

item.title: Man found guilty of starting deadly LA wildfire
item.description:
Jonathan Rinderknecht is found guilty of starting the deadly Palisades fire in Los Angeles, which displaced thousands of people and became one of the most destructive fires in the city’s history. Also: Donald Trump describes his relationship with the leaders of Russia and China as “fantastic”, after meeting with them in Shenzhen. The US president also threatens a ban on American firms building AI data centres overseas, saying they must stay in the US. Russian drones continue to attack Ukraine, with Poland caught in the crossfire. Students in more than 20 European countries protest over education, climate change and military conscription. Cyber security experts in the UK conduct a highly secretive operation to protect its fridges and freezers. Cincinnati Zoo announces the death of the beloved hippo, Fiona. The BBC speaks to the stars of the latest The Hunger Games franchise series, and Christmas comes early for residents in an English town in the form of wrapped cars.

item.title: Abusers convicted in Joanne Young case echoing Pelicot
item.description:
In the first trial of its kind in England, four men have been convicted of raping and sexually abusing a British woman, in a harrowing case that bears similarities to that of Gisèle Pelicot in France. Like Pelicot, Joanne Young chose to allow her name to be made public, after discovering that her then-husband had advertised her online to strangers for sex, repeatedly drugged her and raped her. British police sought the expertise of French investigators on the Pelicot case to assist them in bringing Young's former husband and her other abusers to justice.

Also: AI tech giant Anthropic becomes one of the world's most valuable public companies after its stock market debut. Meanwhile Meta says it is ''re-evaluating'' its 2030 climate goals as the demand for AI data centres drives up emissions. A spacecraft that has been on an eight year journey through outer space is set to enter orbit around Mercury. We hear the Ukrainian view on the face-to-face meeting between Donald Trump, Vladimir Putin and Xi Jinping. Islam is expected to surpass Christianity as the world’s largest religion by 2035. We meet the winner of the International Children's Peace Prize, 17-year-old Colombian climate activist Francisco Vera Manzanares. And who are the candidates challenging Fifa President Gianni Infantino for the top job in world football?

item.title: UN court says Myanmar committed genocide against Rohingyas
item.description:
The International Court of Justice finds Myanmar guilty of genocide against its Rohingya Muslim minority. It's the first such ruling against a state by the court. The ICJ rejected Myanmar’s argument that it had responded to insurgent attacks.

Also: the presidents of China, the US and Russia stress the importance of stable energy flows, UN reform and the prevention of nuclear proliferation at a trilateral summit, internet access is cut in South Korean exam halls, amid fears of cheating. And a remarkable discovery reveals that 125,000 years ago hippos roamed what is now the vast Arabian Desert.

item.title: BBC reports from Ukraine's undergound frontier
item.description:
We go inside the old Soviet-era gas pipeline where Ukraine is fighting an underground war with Russia. The BBC is the first international broadcaster to enter the tunnels where this subterranean battle is taking place. Also: the AI giant Anthropic is set to raise more than 80 billion dollars in its initial public offering, breaking a record set by SpaceX. President Trump pushes back against global regulation of ''Super Intelligence'' - or AI - at the APEC summit in Shenzhen ahead of his meeting with Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin. The US defence secretary Pete Hegseth signs a military cooperation deal with America's former foe Venezuela. Democrats in the US House of Representatives nominate Hakeem Jeffries as first African American Speaker. A new study suggests a pill that mimics Viagra can slow cognitive decline in people with Alzheimer’s disease by almost a third. Rare footage from Brazil shows about 20 Indigenous men and boys emerging from their self-imposed isolation deep in the Amazon rainforest. And a painting by Vincent Van Gogh sells at auction in New York for over 190 million dollars - a record for work by the artist.

item.title: Trump, Xi and Putin meet in China
item.description:
President Trump was greeted by President Xi Jinping at the airport as he arrived in Shenzhen for a summit of Asia-Pacific leaders, which will culminate in a closely-watched meeting on Thursday between the pair and the Russian president. In a highly choreographed moment, Trump and Xi shook hands on the tarmac. Later the US leader met Mr Putin ahead of a gala dinner.

Also: Thousands of people in Haiti have marched in the capital in support of troops from El Salvador, who've been deployed to confront the island's powerful criminal gangs. The Democrats have taken Alaska from the Republicans in the final senate race of the US midterms, nearly three weeks after election day. We hear from a former child refugee from South Sudan, who has walked the entire length of the UK to draw attention to the war in Sudan. And - after more than 13 years, GTA 6 - the latest instalment of the multi billion dollar video game franchise is released amid huge fanfare and expectation.

item.title: Special episode: Trump, Putin and Xi meeting
item.description:
This special episode of the Global News Podcast brings together our China specialist, our North America correspondent, and our Russia and Ukraine analyst, to discuss an unprecedented summit taking place this week. The US President Donald Trump, Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping are due to meet in Shenzhen, China, for their first-ever trilateral talks. President Trump has said the agenda will include denuclearisation, the war with Iran, and the war in Ukraine. So what could emerge from this meeting? Some analysts are hopeful that China could exert some influence on Tehran, and act as a mediator between Moscow and Kyiv. But Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky has said he's worried that the three leaders could try to reshape the international order as they see fit, without consulting smaller countries. Trump, Putin and Xi are also expected to talk about the economy and AI, particularly after Jensen Huang was ousted as CEO of Nvidia, following allegations that he had an affair with a suspected Chinese spy. But will any big decisions come out of the talks in Shenzhen? Or is this about symbolism: a way for the leaders of China, the US and Russia to give themselves a boost and a distraction from their problems at home?

President Trump has said the agenda will include denuclearisation, the war with Iran, and the war in Ukraine. So what could emerge from this meeting? Some analysts are hopeful that China could exert some influence on Tehran, and act as a mediator between Moscow and Kyiv. But Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky has said he's worried that the three leaders could try to reshape the international order as they see fit, without consulting smaller countries. Trump, Putin and Xi are also expected to talk about the economy and AI, particularly after Jensen Huang was ousted as CEO of Nvidia, following allegations that he had an affair with a suspected Chinese spy. But will any big decisions come out of the talks in Shenzhen? Or is this about symbolism: a way for the leaders of China, the US and Russia to give themselves a boost and a distraction from their problems at home?

item.title: The Global Story: How North Korea pulled off a $6bn heist

Kyiv says a ceasefire must come before any discussions on territory, while Moscow demands Ukrainian forces withdraw from parts of eastern Ukraine. Also: widespread disruption hits Spain during the country's first general strike in 14 years, prompted by housing shortages and the high cost of living. Will the UN's climate summit make much impact when the world's biggest emitters have declined to join? item.title: How US model agencies helped Epstein access victims
item.description:
A BBC investigation uncovers new evidence about how model agencies, scouts and powerful fashion figures helped Jeffrey Epstein gain access to young women after his conviction for sex offences. A woman raped by the financier says the president of her model agency put her in danger when he sent her to two photoshoots at Epstein's Florida beach house. At the time, in 2009, Epstein was serving a jail sentence for sex offences against a minor but was allowed to work each day from his home.

Also: dozens of soldiers in the eastern Democratic Republic of Congo are sentenced to death by a military court for offences including cowardice and mutiny. Negotiators from Ukraine, Russia and the US begin two days of talks in Abu Dhabi, aimed at ending the war. One of Russia's few independent news outlets, Novaya Gazeta, is shut down. item.title: Trump backs Hegseth as he faces impeachment push
item.description:
President Trump has said the resumption of US strikes against Iran is "quite unlikely and unnecessary". He expressed support for his defence secretary, Pete Hegseth, after a Republican Congressman, Thomas Massie, introduced articles of impeachment against him for waging war in Iran and elsewhere without Congressional approval. Also: President Trump says the FBI is investigating claims that Jensen Huang, the boss of the US tech giant Nvidia, had an affair with a suspected Chinese agent. He said he'd spoken to Mr Huang - who'd told him he had no idea that the woman was a spy. France has accused Iran of being behind cyberattacks last month that heated up supermarket fridges and freezers, spoiling millions of dollars' worth of food. The former British comedian and actor, Russell Brand is beginning a prison sentence of ten-and-a-half years for raping one woman and sexually assaulting three others between 2004 and 2009. We have a special report from the Libyan city of Derna, which has been rebuilt after Storm Daniel triggered the worst flood disaster in the world this century. Astronomers say the Earth has another temporary moon that's fallen into our planet's gravitational pull. And the author M John Harrison is awarded the prestigious Booker Prize for his dystopian novel, The End of Everything.
